headline: Stress feedback on contractile fibers yields bistability and orthogonal fiber domains
label: Mechanics Driven Tissue Patterning
summary: Recent preprints connect stress feedback and deformability to mechanical structure, now including imaging-calibrated models of wing disc morphogenesis.
synthesis: The common thread is explicit mechanical modeling in which force organizes tissue structure. Two preprints on active elastic tissue show that stress feedback on contractile fibers produces bistable strain responses and orthogonally aligned fiber domains, including around a pressurized lumen in the muscle tissue model. A third preprint uses the Fourier Contour Cell model to show that deformability and self-propulsion shape bimodal intercellular contact-force distributions. A fourth, the MORPHIOME multiscale framework calibrated with imaging data, resolves a mechanical sequence driving Drosophila wing disc eversion, including ECM contributions. What is new is the pairing of feedback-driven patterning theory with calibration to imaging data, linking mechanical instability models to measured morphogenesis. The thread is dominant rather than universal, since the cell-contact study and the wing study address different scales and questions.
